messages.content: Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.
Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.

samples.text: Floating-point numbers have a finite precision, so each operation rounds the exact real‑valued sum to the nearest representable value. Because rounding can discard low‑order bits, the intermediate result of \((a+b)+c\) may lose information that would affect the final sum, while \(a+(b+c)\) rounds a different intermediate value and can retain different bits. Consequently the two rounded results can differ, showing that floating‑point addition does not satisfy the associative law.
